components.note: A drawing of a long, coiling creature with a horned head, representing the mythical Chinese dragon.
虫 (insect/small creature) — 虾 names a small water creature.
下 (xià) gives a sound close to 虾's reading xiā, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的龙虾非常新鲜。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de lóngxiā fēicháng xīnxiān.
example.english: This restaurant's lobster is very fresh.
example.fact: American lobsters can live for over 100 years and keep growing throughout their lives, molting their hard exoskeleton dozens of times along the way. Contrary to popular belief they are not biologically immortal — molting becomes more frequent and energetically costly with age, and the strain of shedding an old shell eventually kills them.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — a bundle of grass or straw carried as a load
力 (strength) — the effort of lifting and carrying the heavy load
马 (horse) shows 驾 relates to driving or controlling an animal or vehicle.
加 (jiā) gives a sound close to jià, differing mainly in tone.

example.hanzi: 劳驾,借过一下。
example.pinyin: Láojià, jiè guò yíxià.
example.english: Excuse me, let me get through.
example.fact: In the 1960s, American anthropologist Edward T. Hall coined the term 'personal space' after observing how much distance people from different cultures kept from one another during conversation. His research founded the field of proxemics, which studies how spatial behavior and comfort zones vary across cultures.

components.note: 平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
土 (earth) — 均 relates to leveling land evenly.
匀 (yún) gives a rhyme close to jūn, with the initial shifted.

example.hanzi: 这个班的平均成绩是八十五分。
example.pinyin: Zhège bān de píngjūn chéngjì shì bāshíwǔ fēn.
example.english: This class's average grade is 85 points.
example.fact: The commonly cited 'normal' human body temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) comes from an 1851 study by German physician Carl Wunderlich, who averaged readings from 25,000 patients. Later studies using modern digital thermometers put the true average closer to 36.6°C, suggesting average human body temperature may have also genuinely cooled over the past 150 years.

components.note: 虍 (tiger) pictures a big cat.
业 pictures tall grass or a hilltop, together suggesting a hollow, empty den — giving 虚 its meaning 'empty, false.'
弓 here pictures a young, bent shoot rather than a bow.
冫 (ice/frost) repeated twice suggests two young shoots wilting in the cold, giving 弱 its meaning 'weak, fragile.'

example.hanzi: 手术后他的身体很虚弱。
example.pinyin: Shǒushù hòu tā de shēntǐ hěn xūruò.
example.english: After the surgery, his body was very weak.
example.fact: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station can lose up to 1-2% of their bone mass per month in microgravity, roughly ten times the rate seen in osteoporosis on Earth. Without gravity to work against, muscles and bones weaken quickly, which is why astronauts exercise about two hours a day to counteract the effect.

components.note: 目 depicts an eye turned on its side, with the outline and pupil visible — later straightened into today's rectangular shape.
白 (white, bright) — 的 originally named a bright spot used as an archery target.
勺 (sháo) is close in sound to 的's reading dí, the character's older pronunciation as 'target.'
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'

example.hanzi: 我们的目的地是长城。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen de mùdìdì shì Chángchéng.
example.english: Our destination is the Great Wall.
example.fact: Point Nemo, in the South Pacific, is the location on Earth farthest from any land — over 2,600 km from the nearest coastline in every direction. Because it is so remote, space agencies use it as a 'spacecraft cemetery,' deliberately crashing decommissioned satellites and space station modules there to avoid populated areas.

meanings: to force sb to do sth

components.note: 力 (strength) — making an effort is tied to exerting strength.
免 (miǎn) gives the sound — an exact match for 勉.
弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.

example.hanzi: 他勉强通过了考试。
example.pinyin: Tā miǎnqiǎng tōngguò le kǎoshì.
example.english: He barely passed the exam.
example.fact: Photosynthesis is famously inefficient: even highly productive crop plants convert only about 1-2% of the sunlight hitting their leaves into stored chemical energy, with most of the rest lost as heat or reflected away. Scientists are researching ways to genetically boost that efficiency to help increase crop yields as the global population grows.

components.note: 辶 (to walk, move) — the traditional form 這 combined this with a phonetic element to mean 'to approach,' a sense later borrowed for the demonstrative 'this.'
文 replaces the original phonetic 言 in the simplified form, keeping only a loose visual echo of the traditional character 這.
页 (head) — 项 originally referred to the back of the neck, near the head, later extended to mean 'item, sum'
工 (gōng) gives a loose sound connection to 项's reading xiàng

example.hanzi: 这项政策将从下个月开始实行。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè jiāng cóng xià ge yuè kāishǐ shíxíng.
example.english: This policy will take effect starting next month.
example.fact: The Code of Hammurabi, carved into a stone stele around 1754 BC in ancient Babylon, contains 282 laws covering trade, property, and family disputes. It is one of the oldest deciphered legal codes of significant length ever discovered, and offers a rare direct window into how an ancient society tried to formally regulate everyday life.

components.note: 冫 (from 水, water) — the full form 決 relates to a river breaking through a barrier, extended to mean 'to resolve, decide.'
夬 (jué) matches the sound of 决 exactly.
斗 depicts a hand-held dipper or ladle used for measuring grain and liquids — giving 斗 its meaning 'a unit of dry measure,' and by extension, the Big Dipper constellation.

example.hanzi: 两位骑士为了荣誉进行了一场决斗。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi qíshì wèile róngyù jìnxíng le yī chǎng juédòu.
example.english: The two knights fought a duel for honor.
example.fact: Dueling with pistols was legal or widely tolerated in much of Europe and the United States well into the 19th century. U.S. Vice President Aaron Burr famously killed former Treasury Secretary Alexander Hamilton in an 1804 duel in Weehawken, New Jersey — a death that helped turn American public opinion against the practice.

components.note: 力 (strength/effort) — the exertion behind the achievement.
工 (work/labor) — results produced through skillful labor, giving 功 its meaning 'achievement, merit, skill.'
讠 (speech) — 课 relates to lessons taught through spoken instruction.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound distantly related to kè, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我每天放学后先做功课。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān fàngxué hòu xiān zuò gōngkè.
example.english: Every day after school, I do my homework first.
example.fact: A large 2006 Duke University meta-analysis of homework research found only a weak link between homework and achievement in elementary school, with the correlation strengthening substantially by high school. This suggests the ideal amount of homework may depend heavily on a student's age and grade level rather than following one universal rule.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines, streaks) — 彩 relates to patterns and bright colors.
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — an exact match with 彩's reading cǎi.
虫 (insect) — ancient people once imagined the rainbow as a giant insect or serpent arching across the sky.
工 (gōng) gives a sound close to hóng, sharing the same rhyme though the initial has shifted.

example.hanzi: 雨后天空出现了一道美丽的彩虹。
example.pinyin: Yǔ hòu tiānkōng chūxiàn le yī dào měilì de cǎihóng.
example.english: After the rain, a beautiful rainbow appeared in the sky.
example.fact: A rainbow is not a fixed object hanging in the sky but a personal optical effect: each observer sees a slightly different rainbow, formed by their own unique cone of sunlight refracting through raindrops at just the right angle relative to their eyes. That is why no one can ever walk to the 'end' of a rainbow — it constantly repositions itself as the observer moves.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — ties to harmony as speaking together in accord
禾 (hé, grain) gives the sound — matches 和's pronunciation hé
讠 (speech) — 谐 relates to getting along well, through agreeable speech or action.
皆 (jiē) gives a sound only distantly related to xié today, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 邻居之间应该和谐相处。
example.pinyin: Línjū zhījiān yīnggāi héxié xiāngchǔ.
example.english: Neighbors should live together harmoniously.
example.fact: Musical harmony traces back to the ancient Greek mathematician Pythagoras, who found around the 6th century BC that pleasing musical intervals correspond to simple numerical ratios between string lengths — a string exactly half as long, for instance, produces a note one octave higher. The discovery linked mathematics and music for the first time in recorded history.

components.note: 日 depicts the sun as a circle with a dot or short stroke inside — a simplified picture of the sun's disc, later squared off in the standard script.
禾 (grain) — 程 originally named a unit for measuring grain, extended to 'process, journey, degree.'
呈 (chéng) gives the sound — 程 is also pronounced chéng, an exact match.

example.hanzi: 请把这次会议加入你的日程。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè cì huìyì jiārù nǐ de rìchéng.
example.english: Please add this meeting to your schedule.
example.fact: The 24-hour day and 60-minute hour used to structure schedules worldwide trace back to ancient Babylonian and Egyptian astronomy, which relied on a base-60 (sexagesimal) counting system. That same ancient system is also why a circle is divided into 360 degrees and a minute contains 60 seconds today.

meanings: (in reference to a person) role model

components.note: 木 (wood) — in old times, notices were posted on wooden boards.
旁 (beside, attached) — combined with wood, the picture is of a notice board posted up for public view, giving 榜 its meaning 'list, placard' (as in an exam results list).
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 老师是学生的榜样。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī shì xuésheng de bǎngyàng.
example.english: Teachers are role models for students.
example.fact: Psychologist Albert Bandura's famous 1961 'Bobo doll' experiment showed that children readily imitate adult behavior they observe, even aggressive actions, simply from watching rather than being directly taught. The study became key early evidence for social learning theory and the powerful influence role models have on behavior.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
扌 (hand) — 报 relates to taking action against someone.
卩 (a kneeling or bound person) — handling a wrongdoer and announcing the judgment gave 报 its meaning 'to report' or 'to announce.'
尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'

example.hanzi: 他在情报局工作了二十年。
example.pinyin: Tā zài qíngbàojú gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
example.english: He worked at the intelligence bureau for twenty years.
example.fact: The CIA's wartime predecessor, the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), was created in 1942 partly on the advice of British intelligence services already fighting Nazi Germany. Its work in sabotage, espionage, and code-breaking support during World War II laid much of the groundwork for the modern American intelligence community that followed.

components.note: 用 is thought to depict a wooden bucket or fence, or possibly a tortoise shell held over a fire during divination. Either way, the everyday act shown in the picture gave the character its meaning 'to use, apply.'
心 was originally a pictograph of the physical shape of a human heart, and came to represent the mind, feelings, and intention as well.

example.hanzi: 她用心地照顾生病的父亲。
example.pinyin: Tā yòngxīn de zhàogù shēngbìng de fùqīn.
example.english: She attentively cared for her sick father.
example.fact: A landmark study published in JAMA in 2011 linked lower nurse-to-patient staffing ratios in hospitals to measurably reduced patient mortality across hundreds of facilities, underscoring how attentive, careful nursing care can directly affect recovery outcomes, not just comfort.

components.note: The traditional form 關 pictured a wooden bolt or bar laid across a pair of double doors, giving the meaning 'to shut, close.' The simplified 关 keeps only a schematic trace of the gate and crossbar.
灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 谢谢你一直关照我。
example.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ yīzhí guānzhào wǒ.
example.english: Thank you for always looking after me.
example.fact: Emperor penguin fathers look after their eggs almost single-handedly, incubating them on their feet under a warm skin fold called a brood pouch for about two months through the Antarctic winter, without eating, while the mothers travel to the sea to feed.

components.note: 气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
自 (nose) — the breath passing through.
心 (heart) — the breath of life, giving 息 its meaning 'to breathe; to rest; news.'

example.hanzi: 春天的空气中弥漫着花的气息。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān de kōngqì zhōng mímàn zhe huā de qìxī.
example.english: In spring, the air is filled with the scent of flowers.
example.fact: A 2014 Rockefeller University study found that the human nose can distinguish over one trillion different odors, far exceeding earlier estimates of around 10,000. Each individual scent is detected through combinations of roughly 400 different types of olfactory receptors.

components.note: 匕 here relates to a person crouching or sitting — 此 originally pictured 'this place' where someone is.
止 (zhǐ) gives a hint of the sound — 此 is pronounced cǐ, sharing a similar final though the initial has shifted over time.
夕 (evening, night) — divination was traditionally done in the evening.
卜 (to divine, reading cracks in bone or shell) — combined with 夕 (evening), an evening divination was for unusual or 'outside' matters, giving 外 its meaning of 'outside' or 'foreign.'

example.hanzi: 此外,我们还需要准备一些饮料。
example.pinyin: Cǐwài, wǒmen hái xūyào zhǔnbèi yīxiē yǐnliào.
example.english: Besides, we also need to prepare some drinks.
example.fact: Mathematician Georg Cantor proved in the 1870s that infinity comes in different sizes: the infinite set of real numbers is strictly 'larger' than the infinite set of whole numbers, even though both sets go on forever. The discovery, once controversial among his peers, is now a foundational result in set theory.

components.note: Thread — suggests something twisted or entangled.
Depicts two threads winding around each other, hence 'entangle.'
一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'

example.hanzi: 老师纠正了我的发音错误。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiūzhèng le wǒ de fāyīn cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher corrected my pronunciation mistake.
example.fact: Modern eyeglasses trace back to 13th-century Italy, where craftsmen in Pisa ground convex glass lenses set in frames to help farsighted readers see fine print. Concave lenses for correcting nearsightedness followed roughly two centuries later, in the 15th century.

components.note: 巨 depicts a hand gripping a large carpenter's square, a tool for measuring right angles — an image linked to great size, giving 巨 its meaning 'huge, giant.'
日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng

example.hanzi: 他从小城市男孩成长为国际巨星。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo chéngshì nánhái chéngzhǎng wéi guójì jùxīng.
example.english: He grew from a small-town boy into an international superstar.
example.fact: The red giant star Betelgeuse, in the constellation Orion, is roughly 700 times the diameter of the Sun — so large that if placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend past the orbit of Jupiter. Astronomers expect it to end its life in a supernova sometime within the next 100,000 years.

components.note: The traditional form 亂 pictured a tangle of thread being pulled apart by a hand-hook, a picture of disorder that gave 乱 its meaning 'chaotic, in disarray.' The simplified form keeps only a trace of that tangled shape.
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.

example.hanzi: 别乱动这些实验器材。
example.pinyin: Bié luàndòng zhèxiē shíyàn qìcái.
example.english: Don't fiddle with this lab equipment.
example.fact: Brownian motion — the seemingly random jittering of tiny particles suspended in a fluid — was explained mathematically by Albert Einstein in a landmark 1905 paper, which showed the erratic movement was caused by countless collisions with individual water molecules. It provided some of the first direct physical evidence that atoms and molecules actually exist.

components.note: 赫 shows 赤 (red) twice, side by side — an intense, blazing red or glow, giving 赫 its meaning 'bright, radiant, illustrious.'

The traditional form 爾 is thought to have depicted an ornamented window lattice or a decorated bow. That original picture was borrowed early on to write the unrelated pronoun 'you, that,' which is the only sense the simplified 尔 keeps today.

example.hanzi: 赫尔是英国东北部的一座港口城市。
example.pinyin: Hè'ěr shì Yīngguó dōngběibù de yī zuò gǎngkǒu chéngshì.
example.english: Hull is a port city in northeastern England.
example.fact: Kingston upon Hull was the birthplace of William Wilberforce, the British politician whose decades-long campaign in Parliament led to the Slave Trade Act of 1807, banning the slave trade throughout the British Empire.

components.note: 屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 他生来就有一副好嗓子。
example.pinyin: Tā shēnglái jiù yǒu yī fù hǎo sǎngzi.
example.english: He was born with a good voice.
example.fact: Human infants are born with a startle reflex called the Moro reflex, an automatic response to sudden movement or loud noise that makes them fling out their arms and legs. It is present from birth and normally fades by around four to six months of age as the nervous system matures.

components.note: 木 (tree) — the traditional form 條 named a slender tree branch, later extended to any long, thin strip and to the measure word for items such as clauses or laws.
欠 (to owe/lack) — 款 relates to funds, especially money owed or paid

example.hanzi: 请仔细阅读合同的每一条款。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zǐxì yuèdú hétong de měi yī tiáokuǎn.
example.english: Please read every clause of the contract carefully.
example.fact: The U.S. Constitution's Second Amendment is only 27 words long, yet it has generated more litigation and legal debate than almost any other clause in American law — a reminder that a handful of words in a founding legal document can carry outsized and contested weight for centuries.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.

example.hanzi: 这个国家的教育制度正在改革。
example.pinyin: Zhège guójiā de jiàoyù zhìdù zhèngzài gǎigé.
example.english: This country's education system is being reformed.
example.fact: China's imperial civil service examination system, the keju, ran for roughly 1,300 years, from the Sui dynasty until it was abolished in 1905. It was one of history's earliest large-scale meritocratic institutions, letting men of relatively humble background reach high government office simply by passing rigorous written exams.

meanings: to get out of the way

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 让's meaning 'to let, allow, yield,' something granted through spoken permission.
上 (shàng) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from ràng.
廾 (two hands) — depicts hands at work.
一 represents the latch or bar of a door; hands lifting it away gave 开 its meaning 'to open, to start.'

example.hanzi: 请让开,救护车要过去。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ràngkāi, jiùhùchē yào guòqù.
example.english: Please step aside, an ambulance needs to get through.
example.fact: Ambulance sirens in many countries alternate between two tones because a moving vehicle's sound shifts pitch due to the Doppler effect. The familiar 'hi-lo' pattern was designed to stay audibly distinct and attention-grabbing even as a vehicle's speed and position relative to a listener keep changing.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 纵 originally described letting a thread run loose, extended to mean 'to indulge, release.'
从 (cóng) gives a sound close to zòng.
A pictograph of rising flames — the source of 火's meaning 'fire.'

example.hanzi: 警方正在调查这起纵火案。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhèngzài diàochá zhè qǐ zònghuǒ àn.
example.english: The police are investigating this arson case.
example.fact: Fire investigators can often tell whether a fire was deliberately set by studying burn patterns. Accelerant-fueled arson fires tend to leave distinctive 'pour patterns' and unusually fast, intense burns, and lab techniques like gas chromatography can detect trace chemical residues, such as gasoline, left behind in the debris.

components.note: 十 is thought to derive from a single knot tied in a rope, an ancient counting method where a knot marked a count of ten.
The traditional form 萬 originally depicted a scorpion. That picture was borrowed early on for the large number 'ten thousand,' a meaning that has nothing to do with the original animal.

example.hanzi: 这辆车花了十万元。
example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē huā le shíwàn yuán.
example.english: This car cost a hundred thousand yuan.
example.fact: The human body contains roughly 100,000 kilometers of blood vessels — arteries, veins, and capillaries combined — enough to circle the Earth about two and a half times, all packed into a body typically under two meters tall.

components.note: 氵 (water) shows 澳 relates to a body of water, like a bay or inlet.
奥 (ào) gives the exact sound of 澳.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
禾 (grain, a growing rice or wheat plant) — 利 pictures a harvest.
刂 (knife) — cutting grain at harvest time was a clear benefit or gain, giving 利 its meaning 'profit' or 'advantage.'
A pictograph of a cross-shaped building, possibly an altar or temple floor plan; the character was later adopted to write 'Asia' (亚洲) and the unrelated meaning 'second, next.'

example.hanzi: 澳大利亚有很多独特的野生动物。
example.pinyin: Àodàlìyà yǒu hěnduō dútè de yěshēng dòngwù.
example.english: Australia has many unique wild animals.
example.fact: Australia is the only continent occupied entirely by a single country, and roughly 80% of its mammal, reptile, and frog species occur nowhere else on Earth. That extreme uniqueness stems from millions of years of geographic isolation after Australia broke away from the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.

components.note: 亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
讠 (speech) — 谱 relates to a written or spoken record, like a chart or score.
普 (pǔ) gives the sound — an exact match with 谱.

example.hanzi: 他的要求实在太离谱了。
example.pinyin: Tā de yāoqiú shízài tài lípǔ le.
example.english: His request is really outrageous.
example.fact: Western five-line staff notation, still used by musicians worldwide, was standardized by the 11th century thanks largely to the Italian monk Guido of Arezzo, who also devised the 'do-re-mi' solfège syllables that helped singers learn unfamiliar melodies far more quickly than by ear alone.

components.note: 户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 他投资了不少房产。
example.pinyin: Tā tóuzī le bùshǎo fángchǎn.
example.english: He has invested in a lot of real estate.
example.fact: Antilia, a 27-story private home in Mumbai, is widely reported as the most expensive residential property ever built, with estimated values well over a billion dollars and a staff of around 600 needed to maintain it — illustrating just how far luxury real estate valuations can exceed those of ordinary office towers.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 谋 relates to discussing and forming a plan.
某 (mǒu) gives the sound — an exact match with 谋.
乂 depicts crossed strokes suggesting a cutting action.
木 (wood) here represents a wooden stake — giving 杀 its meaning 'to kill.'
罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net

example.hanzi: 他被指控犯有谋杀罪。
example.pinyin: Tā bèi zhǐkòng fàn yǒu móushāzuì.
example.english: He was accused of committing murder.
example.fact: Forensic DNA fingerprinting was first used to help solve a murder case in 1986, when British geneticist Alec Jeffreys assisted police in identifying a killer in Leicestershire, England. It was the first time genetic evidence secured a criminal conviction, launching the modern era of DNA-based forensic science.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — a hand held out, palm up
乇 — something resting on the upturned palm for support
马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
斤 (axe) — 斯 originally meant 'to split apart' with an axe.
其 is close in sound to 斯's older pronunciation, though the two readings have drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 托马斯是我的好朋友。
example.pinyin: Tuōmǎsī shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.
example.english: Thomas is my good friend.
example.fact: The name Thomas comes from the Aramaic word te'oma, meaning 'twin,' and was borne by the apostle Thomas in the New Testament, often remembered as 'Doubting Thomas' for reportedly refusing to believe in Jesus's resurrection until he could see the physical evidence for himself.

components.note: 羊 depicts a sheep.
次 depicts saliva dripping from an open mouth — paired with the sheep, the image is of someone drooling over a flock of sheep, giving 羡 its meaning 'to envy, admire.'
⺗ (heart) — admiration and longing are feelings of the heart.
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to mù, sharing the initial consonant.

example.hanzi: 我很羡慕她的好口才。
example.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiànmù tā de hǎo kǒucái.
example.english: I really admire her eloquence.
example.fact: Psychologists distinguish 'benign envy,' which motivates people to work harder to attain what someone else has, from 'malicious envy,' which instead makes people wish to see the other person lose it. Research published in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology in 2011 found the two types produce different behaviors and even different facial expressions.

components.note: 攵 (a hand taking action) — 救 describes the act of rescuing someone.
求 (qiú) gives a sound close to jiù, sharing a similar rhyme.
世 depicts three leaves or shoots on a stem, suggesting continuous growth across generations — giving rise to the meaning 'generation' or 'world.'
丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'

example.hanzi: 基督徒相信耶稣是救世主。
example.pinyin: Jīdūtú xiāngxìn Yēsū shì Jiùshìzhǔ.
example.english: Christians believe that Jesus is the Savior.
example.fact: The Christ the Redeemer statue overlooking Rio de Janeiro, completed in 1931, stands 30 meters tall atop Corcovado mountain and is built from reinforced concrete and soapstone. It was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in a global public poll in 2007.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 海 relates to bodies of water, specifically the sea.
每 (měi) gives a hint of the sound — 海 is pronounced hǎi, a connection that has shifted over time.
广 (a building/shelter) — 底 relates to the base or bottom, as of a structure
氐 (dǐ) gives the sound — 底 is also pronounced dǐ, an exact match

example.hanzi: 潜水员在海底发现了一艘沉船。
example.pinyin: Qiánshuǐyuán zài hǎidǐ fāxiàn le yī sōu chénchuán.
example.english: The diver found a sunken ship on the seabed.
example.fact: The Challenger Deep, the lowest known point of the seabed in the Mariana Trench, plunges nearly 11,000 meters below sea level — deep enough to submerge Mount Everest with over 2 kilometers to spare. Only a handful of crewed submersibles have ever reached its bottom.

components.note: Hand — an action done by hand, like pressing down.
Gives the sound áng, related to yì but drifted apart over time.
阝 (from 邑, city) — an old tie to a place name, per its 'city' etymology.
有 (yǒu) gives a sound close in initial to yù, though the rhyme has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 长期的压力可能导致抑郁。
example.pinyin: Chángqī de yālì kěnéng dǎozhì yìyù.
example.english: Long-term stress can lead to depression.
example.fact: The World Health Organization estimates that depression affects more than 280 million people worldwide, making it one of the leading causes of disability globally. Twentieth-century research linking mood to brain chemistry, particularly neurotransmitters like serotonin, helped reshape it from a poorly understood personal weakness into a recognized, treatable medical condition.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侄 names a family member, one's nephew.
至 (zhì) gives a sound close to zhí, the same syllable with a different tone.
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.

example.hanzi: 这是我哥哥的女儿,我的侄女。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ gēge de nǚ'ér, wǒ de zhínǚ.
example.english: This is my older brother's daughter, my niece.
example.fact: Genetically, a niece shares on average 25% of her DNA with an aunt or uncle, the same fraction of shared DNA as between a grandparent and grandchild. This comes from standard rules of human relatedness, since each additional generational or lateral step in a family tree roughly halves the expected genetic overlap.

components.note: 几 depicts a small low table or stool with legs — a simple domestic object.
率 originally depicted a twisted cord or string 幺 being pulled taut in a frame — later extended to meanings like 'to lead' (pulling something along) and 'rate, ratio.'

example.hanzi: 明天下雨的几率很高。
example.pinyin: Míngtiān xiàyǔ de jǐlǜ hěn gāo.
example.english: The probability of rain tomorrow is high.
example.fact: Modern probability theory traces back to a 1654 exchange of letters between French mathematicians Blaise Pascal and Pierre de Fermat, who were trying to settle a gambling dispute over how to fairly divide the stakes of an unfinished game of chance. Their correspondence laid mathematical foundations still used today in insurance, weather forecasting, and statistics.

components.note: 亻 (person) — 健 describes a person's physical condition.
建 depicts building or constructing — a person strong enough to build things gave 健 its meaning 'strong, healthy.'
身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match

example.hanzi: 他每天下班后都去健身房锻炼。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān xiàbān hòu dōu qù jiànshēnfáng duànliàn.
example.english: He goes to the gym to exercise every day after work.
example.fact: The word 'gymnasium' comes from the ancient Greek gymnos, meaning 'naked,' because Greek athletes traditionally trained and competed nude. Ancient gymnasiums were also centers of philosophy and education rather than pure exercise — both Plato's Academy and Aristotle's Lyceum were built around gymnasium complexes in Athens.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 透 relates to moving all the way through something.
秀 (xiù) gives a sound distantly related to tòu, having drifted apart over time.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過

example.hanzi: 阳光透过窗户照进了房间。
example.pinyin: Yángguāng tòuguò chuānghù zhàojìn le fángjiān.
example.english: Sunlight passed through the window into the room.
example.fact: Neutrinos are subatomic particles so weakly interacting that trillions of them pass through the human body every second without any effect. Produced in vast numbers by nuclear reactions inside the Sun, they can pass straight through the entire Earth almost undisturbed, which is why detecting them requires enormous underground tanks shielded from other radiation.

components.note: 犭 (dog) shows 猜 relates to an animal sense used metaphorically for a hunch.
青 (qīng) gives a sound distantly related to cāi, having drifted apart over time.
心 (heart/mind) — 想 relates to thinking, missing someone, or wanting something in one's heart.
相 (xiāng) gives the sound — 想 is pronounced xiǎng, matching aside from tone.

example.hanzi: 科学家们对宇宙的起源提出了各种猜想。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen duì yǔzhòu de qǐyuán tíchū le gèzhǒng cāixiǎng.
example.english: Scientists have proposed various conjectures about the origin of the universe.
example.fact: The Goldbach Conjecture, proposed by mathematician Christian Goldbach in 1742, states that every even integer greater than 2 can be written as the sum of two prime numbers. Despite being verified by computer for numbers up to 4 quintillion without a single exception, it remains unproven and is one of the oldest unsolved problems in mathematics.

components.note: 贝 (shell, an ancient form of money) — 赛 originally related to offering valuables, later coming to mean 'to compete.'
宀 (mián) gives a sound distantly related to sài, having drifted apart over time.
马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.

example.hanzi: 他周末喜欢去看赛马。
example.pinyin: Tā zhōumò xǐhuan qù kàn sàimǎ.
example.english: He likes to watch horse racing on weekends.
example.fact: In 1878, photographer Eadweard Muybridge settled a long-running debate about horse locomotion by using a row of cameras with tripwires to capture a galloping horse frame by frame. The images proved that all four hooves do leave the ground at once, a motion too fast for the naked eye to confirm, and the technique helped launch the development of motion pictures.

components.note: 勹 (an enclosing shape) — wrapping around.
巳 (a baby) — swaddled inside, the image of wrapping something up giving 包 its meaning 'to wrap; bag, package.'
衣 (clothing) — 装 relates to clothes, dress, and attire
壮 (zhuàng) gives the sound — 装 is pronounced zhuāng, a close match

example.hanzi: 这个产品的包装非常精美。
example.pinyin: Zhège chǎnpǐn de bāozhuāng fēicháng jīngměi.
example.english: This product's packaging is very exquisite.
example.fact: Corrugated cardboard, the material behind most modern shipping boxes, was patented in England in 1856 — originally as a liner for tall hats, not for packaging at all. It wasn't adapted for shipping boxes until decades later in the United States, where it quickly replaced heavier wooden crates.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 损 relates to damage or loss caused by an action.
员 (yuán) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading sǔn has diverged.
土 (earth) — 坏 relates to something crumbling or deteriorating, like broken soil.
不 (bù) reflects an old phonetic link that has largely faded in the modern pronunciation huài.

example.hanzi: 地震损坏了很多房屋。
example.pinyin: Dìzhèn sǔnhuài le hěnduō fángwū.
example.english: The earthquake damaged many houses.
example.fact: The 1960 Great Chilean Earthquake, at magnitude 9.5, remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded by modern instruments. It damaged or destroyed roughly two million homes and triggered a tsunami that caused destruction as far away as Hawaii, Japan, and the Philippines.

components.note: 马 (simplified from 馬) depicts a horse in profile, with its mane, legs, and tail visible — later simplified into just a few strokes.
Yawn — associated with tiredness and needing rest.
Gives the sound hé, related to xiē but drifted apart over time.

The traditional form 爾 is thought to have depicted an ornamented window lattice or a decorated bow. That original picture was borrowed early on to write the unrelated pronoun 'you, that,' which is the only sense the simplified 尔 keeps today.

example.hanzi: 马歇尔将军提出了帮助欧洲重建的计划。
example.pinyin: Mǎxiē'ěr jiāngjūn tíchū le bāngzhù Ōuzhōu chóngjiàn de jìhuà.
example.english: General Marshall proposed a plan to help rebuild Europe.
example.fact: The Marshall Plan, officially the European Recovery Program, provided the equivalent of well over 100 billion of today's dollars to rebuild Western European economies after World War II. Its architect, U.S. Secretary of State George Marshall, remains the only career military general ever awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, which he received in 1953.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates directly to 持's meaning 'to hold, maintain.'
寺 (sì) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from chí.
木 (wood) — early spears and rifle stocks were made of wood.
仓 (cāng) gives a sound close to qiāng, sharing the same rhyme.

example.hanzi: 警察持枪进入了大楼。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá chíqiāng jìnrù le dàlóu.
example.english: The police entered the building carrying guns.
example.fact: The AK-47, one of the most widely produced firearms in history with an estimated 75 million-plus units made since 1949, was designed by Soviet engineer Mikhail Kalashnikov. He reportedly said late in life that he wished he had invented something that helped farmers instead, like a lawnmower.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
米 (mǐ) gives a sound close to 咪's reading mī — the same syllable, differing only in tone.
口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
米 (mǐ) gives a sound close to 咪's reading mī — the same syllable, differing only in tone.

example.hanzi: 小猫咪咪地叫着,想要吃东西。
example.pinyin: Xiǎomāo mīmī de jiào zhe, xiǎng yào chī dōngxi.
example.english: The kitten meowed, wanting something to eat.
example.fact: Adult cats rarely meow at each other; researchers believe the behavior is aimed mainly at humans, reinforced over thousands of years of domestication because it reliably gets a person's attention. Kittens meow at their mothers, but most cats largely stop meowing at other cats once grown.

components.note: A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'

example.hanzi: 会议因为停电而中断了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì yīnwèi tíngdiàn ér zhōngduàn le.
example.english: The meeting was interrupted because of a power outage.
example.fact: In computing, a 'hardware interrupt' is a signal that temporarily halts a processor's current task so it can immediately respond to something more urgent, such as a keystroke or an incoming network packet. Developed in the 1950s, the concept let computers react quickly to real-world events instead of constantly checking for them, and it remains fundamental to how virtually every modern computer operates.

components.note: 入 depicts a simple wedge or arrow shape pointing inward, showing the direction of entering.
宀 (roof) — 室 refers to an enclosed room under a roof
至 (zhì) gives the sound — an exact match with 室's reading shì

example.hanzi: 有人入室盗窃了他家的财物。
example.pinyin: Yǒurén rùshì dàoqiè le tā jiā de cáiwù.
example.english: Someone broke into his house and stole his belongings.
example.fact: Studies of residential burglary patterns have found that most break-ins happen during the day rather than at night, when many homes sit empty because occupants are at work or school. The FBI reports that daytime hours, especially between about 10am and 3pm, see disproportionately more residential burglaries than nighttime hours.
